translation: The wrist bone (腕骨) is the palm bone, that is, the proximal segment (本節) of the five fingers, also called the yong bone (壅骨), commonly called the tiger bone (虎骨). Its bones are six in number, large and small, which come together to form the palm; it is not a single solid mass of flesh. At its base it connects above to the ends of the arm and auxiliary bones; the bone on its outer side is called the high bone (高骨), also called the sharp bone (銳骨), also called the ankle bone (踝骨), commonly called the dragon bone (龍骨). Because it can bend and flex up and down, it is therefore called the wrist (腕).
